title: Convergent Physical-Bifolio Structure and Long-Range Model Failure in the Voynich Manuscript
summary: This author manuscript compares predictions for local structure, physical sheets, and longer blocks of Voynich text. Several text and image analyses find associations with physical bifolios, while the most strictly matched text test remains inconclusive. Its normalized reference generator reproduces some local effects and underestimates the variation of token counts across longer blocks.
established: In 3,884 P0 lines, adjacent words were identical in 0.957% of within-line opportunities and 0.194% of opportunities across successive lines on the same folio. The author reports p=0.0002 under a folio-preserving shuffle. Alternative transcriptions are measurements of the same manuscript.

At a matched history length of 640 tokens, bifolio caches gained 0.020, 0.028, and 0.021 bits per token relative to folio caches in the H, C, and F transcriptions. Whole bifolios are the held-out groups in the model comparisons. Nominal gains from unequal history lengths combine physical scope and amount of context.

The H/80-token direct morphology contrast has 46 eligible physical pairs, then 32 exact-distance pairs in 12 quires, then 22 pairs in nine quires after additionally matching hand, Currier class and illustration domain. The last comparison retains a negative mate-minus-control distance of about -0.00857, with p=0.120987901. The complete-metadata sensitivity has 17 pairs in seven quires and p=0.101389861. The stricter text-only test does not establish a separate association.

An analysis of pixels and anonymous word boxes independent of token strings finds stronger mate similarity in measured production features for 41 Voyager and 38 Yale bifolios with both leaves represented. Each conditional p=0.0002 uses random rematching within the quire without exact matching by folio distance, hand, Currier class and domain. The two scans show the same manuscript and share the underlying box coordinate inventory. Registration succeeds on 176/176 eligible Voyager sides and 143/181 eligible Yale sides. The Yale sensitivity requiring two sides per leaf has only 18 complete mates.

At each of five stated widths from 2,810 to 8,430 tokens, the observed H transcription block-variance exponent exceeds all 256 samples from the reference generator. All 16 calibration works exceed the median of both their frequency-preserving shuffle and empirical-bigram controls at every width. The author reports that H exceeds the external calibration range at the primary width and that the widest window leaves only three complete blocks.

The archived inventories contain zero comparable chemical main-text mate pairs. One usable multispectral mate pair, f1r and f8r, ranks seventh by distance among 28 image pairs in the primary 12-band analysis and from seventh to sixteenth in the sensitivity analyses. These public data leave the material explanation unresolved.

open.question: Can a preregistered, independently calibrated production marker distinguish physical bifolio mates from comparable nonmates without using text, known pair labels during feature extraction, or the authors' token-window selection?
open.check: Before scoring, record the eligible pair count from confirmed physical-sheet maps and public scans, including exposed and unobservable image regions and registration losses by side. Define one production marker, require viable same-quire, distance- and capture-quality-matched controls, and compare physical mates with these nonmates at the quire level. Report insufficiency if the prospective matched support fails. Reserve chemical or substrate attribution for a separately calibrated measurement.

open.question: Can a model calibrated on external corpora reproduce the manuscript's block-level exact-token count variation across all five fixed widths while retaining its local held-out performance?
open.check: Fix the model using external texts and public training pages. Freeze the diagnostic widths and the quality gate on length-matched historical texts against exact-frequency shuffle and empirical-bigram controls before comparing the manuscript. Report the observed exponent, model sample range, complete block count, and local predictive score. Retain shared generator tests and preserve quire or sheet grouping when enough complete blocks are available.

evidence.document_status: Open author manuscript dated 12 August 2026, without a verified deposit DOI.
